title: Network CSV rerun WebView operator surface
summary: Phase 7 exposes Network CSV rerun progress, start controls, and destination-policy evidence in WebView using backend-owned read models and command routes only.
reason: Phases 4A through 6 create and process Network CSV rerun rows, but the operator still needs visible progress, row outcome, worker/result evidence, and safe launch controls without moving policy or mutation authority into the frontend.
behavior_before: Network CSV rerun state is backend-readable through existing results/network data, but the WebView has no first-class operator surface for choosing local versus network CSV rerun, inspecting active network rerun batches, or seeing Phase 6 destination-policy outcomes.
behavior_after: WebView surfaces backend-authored Network CSV rerun start/read/status evidence, distinguishes local and network CSV rerun, displays network batch/row progress and destination outcomes, and keeps all claims, policy decisions, filesystem mutation, pending publish, and final placement owned by backend routes.
tests_added: tests.python.desktop.test_application_facade_web_static_queue: Queue local/Network CSV rerun controls, routes, request builders, and backend confirmation payloads
tests.webview.test_webview_network_read_only_boundary: Network page read-only Network CSV rerun panel and backend evidence boundary
tests.webview.test_webview_frontend_mutation_boundary: Network CSV rerun route ownership and confirm_start/fingerprint payload boundary
tests.webview.test_webview_browser_network_smoke: browser-export coverage for Network rerun renderer
tests.python.desktop.test_application_facade_web_static_diagnostics_reports: broad refresh handoff for rerun results
manual_validation: PASS: .\apps\desktop\runtime\Python\python.exe .\ops\scripts\dev\run-python-tool.py mediapipeline.tools.dev.refresh_summaries --changed (15 written, 47 unchanged), then rerun after packet/PREWORK edits (0 written, 62 unchanged)
rollback_plan: Remove or hide the Phase 7 WebView controls/panels while leaving backend Network CSV rerun routes, state files, worker claims, reducer behavior, and destination-policy evidence intact. Do not alter network batch state, pending publish manifests, final outputs, handoff outputs, or source media during UI rollback.
notes:
Phase 7 scope: WebView operator surface only. Backend APIs remain authoritative for start-dry-run, start, results, worker state, command journal, row status, destination policy, and filesystem effects.
D1 primary placement: Queue CSV Rerun tab gets a local/network execution selector and network dry-run/start controls; Network page gets active Network CSV rerun batch/row summary; Home/Live may read summaries from existing results but must not become authoritative.
D2 frontend data source: use existing backend routes first, especially /api/rerun/results for queue/network row state and existing network worker routes for worker posture. Add backend read route only if current data cannot express active batch/row state without frontend inference.
D3 mutation boundary: WebView may post only existing backend command payloads with strict confirmations. It must not author row status, claim rows, destination policy, handoff paths, Pending Publish paths, or final output paths.
D4 display model: render backend status labels, destination_policy_result, reducer/worker evidence, pending manifest paths, published path, review path, and failed-policy messages as evidence. Do not compute clean-versus-review policy in JS.
D5 controls: network start controls must require backend dry-run proof and explicit confirm_start. Future stop/continue controls stay disabled or absent unless backend routes already exist with strict confirmations.
D6 safety UX: use disabled states and backend errors, not extra prompts layered over backend strict confirmations. Read-only preview and evidence views should remain routine operator workflows.
D7 validation: static WebView tests for payload construction/rendering, API contract tests if route payloads change, browser no-mutation smoke if visible controls are added, and inventories/DOM/global exports updated when touched.
D8 stop conditions: stop if WebView would need to compute destination policy, write network batch state directly, mutate filesystem/pending publish/final outputs, infer worker claim status outside backend data, or add frontend-only safety gates that duplicate backend confirmations.
